newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - July 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Business press - July 4.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its contents.
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- MISSISSIPPI WINS $3 BILLION TOBACCO SETTLEMENT

The US state of Mississippi is to receive more than $3 billion from the tobacco industry in settlement of a lawsuit that sought to recover public funds spent treating sick smokers. The settlement came just five days before Mississippi was due to become the first state to face the industry in court. One of the lawyers representing the state, Richard Scruggs, is entitled to 25 percent of the funds recovered, or $750 million.
-- TAXPAYERS COULD PICK UP BILL FOR REGAN DEFENCE

David Sonn, solicitor for former Co-operative Wholesale Society executive Allan Green, has warned that taxpayers may have to pay all the defence costs of Andrew Regan and David Lyons, the failed bidders for CWS, if the Society's prosecutions fail. The prosecutions, which were adjourned on Thursday for seven weeks, allege that Regan and Lyons encouraged Green to steal confidential CWS documents to help them with their bid.
-- PROBE INTO MACKIE LOSS

Sul Sahota, the new chief executive of troubled Northern Ireland textiles machinery firm Mackie International, has said that the company has terminated the contracts of its former chairman Pat Dougan and finance director Shaun Harte. The move comes after Mackie was forced to restate last year's 440,000 stg loss to 7 million stg this year in a document for a share rescue rights issue. Sahota also said the company has asked its new lawyers, Slaughter & May, to investigate the events that led to the restatement.
THE TIMES
-- BUDGET SENDS SHARES TO NEW HIGH

Shares on the London Stock Exchange soared on Thursday as dealers reacted positively to the summer budget. The FTSE 100 index of leading shares closed up 80.3 points at 4831.7, the biggest bounce yet following a budget. Investors are expecting the High Street spending boom to continue after the Chancellor decided against targeting consumers with higher taxes. However, speculation is mounting that the Bank of England is set to raise interest rates next week, and the rumours helped the pound surge to a six-year high against the German mark.
-- LOCKHEED MENACES EUROPE WITH BIG MERGER

The world's leading defence group, Lockheed Martin, is to complete an 11.6 million dollar merger with its US rival Northrop Grumman. The merger is seen as the completion of consolidation in the American aerospace industry and is expected to pose a major commercial threat to European manufacturers. The reported final incentive for the deal was the 13 billion dollar merger between McDonnell Douglas and Boeing, a deal currently being reviewed by the European Commission. European competition commissioner Karel van Miert is considering an investigation into the Lockheed deal.
-- MIRROR TO UNVEIL BID FOR MIDLAND TITLES

The Mirror Group, which publishes The Mirror, Daily Record and The Sporting Life, is believed to be in preparations to make an agreed 285 million sterling bid for Midland Independent Newspapers. MIN is the UK's sixth-largest regional newspaper company in terms of circulation and should Mirror purchase it, as is expected to occur on Friday, it will be the group's first entry into regional newspapers south of Scotland.
THE GUARDIAN
-- US FIRMS 'WINNING THE EURO BATTLE'

A survey of financial institutions, conducted by IT and management consultants Cap Gemini, has found that American firms are set to do better than their European counterparts when the single currency is introduced. The study claimed that insurance firms based in Europe have hugely underestimated the preparation and costs of monetary union. The consultancy claimed that by contrast, US institutions with significant operations in Europe were 'aggressively' preparing for the single currency.
-- NORTHERN FOODS' BOSS GETS LABOUR NOD

Christopher Haskins, chairman of Northern Foods, has been appointed head of the government's new 'Better Regulation' taskforce. The new 40-strong unit has been charged with the task of revamping business regulatory policies, developing proposals to 'improve the effectiveness and credibility of government regulation by ensuring that it is necessary, fair and affordable'.
-- BACK TO OLD TIME FOR SAINSBURY

Figures from the Institute of Grocery Distribution, the trade body of the grocery industry, show that Sainsbury bounced back last year to regain the market share it held before the slump of 1995-96. The data claimed all four of the leading supermarkets gained market share last year, dispelling the theory that one company's gains must be at the expense of its immediate rivals. Among the losers were Kwik Save, ceding 0.1 of a percentage point of market share, and Somerfield, losing 0.2 of a point.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- UTILITY SHARES BOUNCE BACK

Shares in utility companies rose on the stock market on Thursday despite the announcement of the 'windfall tax' in Wednesday's Budget. Dealers welcomed the fact that the higher-than-expected levy payments for water and gas businesses would be a 'one-off'. According to one utilities analyst, Angela Whelan of Credit Lyonnais, 'the key thing is not the scale of the tax, but the removal of uncertainty'.
-- ELECTRICITY PRICES TO DROP BY 12 PERCENT

Offer, the watchdog for the UK electricity industry, has said household electricity bills should fall by 12 percent from next April. The fall is expected as power groups pass on cheaper coal contracts and lower supply and distribution charges. Industry regulator Professor Stephen Littlechild has also revealed details of a new price formula due to be rolled out for the staggered start of domestic power competition from next April.
-- BAA PAYS 406 MILLION STG FOR US DUTY-FREE GIANT

British Airports Authority (BAA), which owns London's Heathrow and Gatwick airports, has announced an agreed bid of 406 million stg for US duty-free business Duty Free International (DFI). The deal will elevate BAA into second place in the world's $20 billion tax-free shopping market, and means that retailing will account for up to 60 percent of BAA's revenues.
